provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
Canonical mechanism: solid rectangles hang from one edge, separated by single background lines, and they start at one end of that edge. The output has a fixed depth of 10 across the hanging axis. Its length along the sequence is the sum of the long sides plus n-1. The output holds two bands. The first lies against the hanging edge: each box is laid flat (long side along the edge, short side as depth), and boxes are spaced long+1 apart. The second stands against the opposite edge: each box is upright (long side as depth, short side along the edge), and boxes are spaced short+1 apart. Both bands start from the same end.

For each D4 view, the factory works out three things in visible coordinates: which visible edge is the hanging edge, whether the sequence runs along columns or rows, and which end the order starts from. It does this by tracking the canonical 'down' and 'right' vectors through the row reversal and the clockwise rotations.

The emitted program scans the visible lines across the sequence, in sequence order. It reads each line from the hanging edge and counts the leading foreground cells. Runs of non-zero depth become boxes, with width = run length and height = maximum depth. It then paints both bands directly into the visible output with orientation-specific index arithmetic. It does not rotate any grid.

Colours are inferred from pixels, so the palette argument is not needed. The foreground is the colour of the visible corner where the hanging edge meets the start of the sequence; the generator always puts a box there. The background is the other colour. This deliberately replaces the archived solver's 'most common colour = background' heuristic. That heuristic fails on valid generated scenes where the foreground covers most of the input, for example several wide boxes of height 1.
draft_notes.limitations: The output depth uses the generator constant 10. It is raised only if a box's long side would exceed it, which cannot happen in the generator's domain. Boxes are segmented as runs of lines that have foreground at the hanging edge. This relies on the generator's guarantees: boxes are separated by exactly one background line and are flush with the hanging edge. The generator can produce grids wider than 30 (up to 6 boxes with long sides up to 6). The program does not enforce ARC size limits. Constructor note for host review: the archived solver chooses the background as the most common colour, which misidentifies the colours on foreground-dominated generated inputs. This is a solver defect, not a puzzle rule, and it is not reproduced here. No fixture contradictions were found. All three train pairs and the test pair are consistent with the rule, and the corner-based colour inference matches them.
draft_notes.host_review: Host read complete constructor and factory. Source rectangles are recovered by separated runs from the specialized hanging edge. Output paints landscape copies along one edge and portrait copies along the opposite edge, retaining order. Rejection sampling preserves 4-6 boxes and their dimensions while enforcing <=30 output width.

repair_verification.independent_review: Host source review; no additional CLI review claimed.
